payload.title: Make optimization runs self-identifying in operator views
payload.description:
As an optimization operator, I want every optimization run to identify its kind, human-readable scope, and current lifecycle state from the Procedure dashboard through the living Report, so that I can distinguish concurrent work without opening raw evidence.

Included:
- Distinguish account-wide portfolio, scorecard-scoped portfolio, and single-score optimization identities.
- Use human-readable scorecard and score names in operator presentation.
- Apply one consistent identity to Procedure, Task, Report title/subtitle, and Report cover.
- Show the current lifecycle phase and status separately from the durable run identity.
- Preserve opaque IDs only in machine evidence and validated responses.

Excluded:
- New GraphQL models, indexes, associations, storage, or infrastructure.
- Automatic score mutation, evaluation, promotion, or feedback-setting changes.
- Client-specific naming rules.

Feature: Self-identifying optimization runs

Scenario: Account-wide portfolio run is recognizable
  Given an optimization run covers every eligible scorecard
  When an operator views the Procedures dashboard or its living Report
  Then the run is labeled as an account-wide portfolio optimization
  And its current lifecycle phase and status are visible

Scenario: Scorecard-scoped portfolio run is recognizable
  Given an optimization run is limited to one or more scorecards
  When an operator views the Procedures dashboard or its living Report
  Then the run is labeled as a scorecard-scoped portfolio optimization
  And the human-readable scope is shown without opaque identifiers

Scenario: Single-score run is recognizable
  Given an optimization run targets exactly one score
  When an operator views the Procedures dashboard or its living Report
  Then the run is labeled as a single-score optimization
  And the human-readable scorecard and score names are shown

Scenario: Identity remains stable while progress changes
  Given a living optimization run advances through analysis, approval, execution, and review
  When each durable milestone is published
  Then the run identity and URL remain stable
  And only the lifecycle phase, status, progress, and next checkpoint change

Scenario: Presentation remains safe
  Given the run evidence contains opaque identifiers and restricted details
  When operator-facing identity is rendered
  Then raw identifiers and restricted evidence are not exposed
  And no new backend resource is required
